text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected in prod (p99 latency > 2.5s) for streaming endpoints in eu-west-2. Auto-routing fallback triggered. Creating incident INC-2026-0421. Paging oncall.

alex: saw the bot — p95 also creeping up from 180ms to ~700ms over the last 10m. Streaming stalls reported by customers on long-poll endpoints.

maya: confirmed. Grafana shows a clear divergence between eu-west-2 and us-west-2. eu-west-2 p99 at ~3.1s, tail spikes correlate with router errors: "no-route" / 502 from lb.

jordan: any recent config rollouts for routing policies? I saw a deploy to router-policy service ~8m ago (canary).

sam: that canary was the weight-reshuffle patch to prefer local shards for affinity (PR #4823). Rollout started 12m ago.

reyes: pulling logs. Router logs from a subset of nodes show repeated: "policy-match: bucket-not-found, falling back" and heavy retry loops. That will amplify tail latency.

alex: sounds like a policy misassignment -> hot partitioning where some shards get overloaded. Can we revert the policy quickly?

maya: recommend pausing rollout and reverting immediately if we see correlation. Oncall, can you confirm you were paged? @oncall-bot

oncall-bot: Oncall acknowledged: paging reyes. Oncall is en route. Escalation to eng-sre if not ACK in 4m.

reyes: I'm on it. I'm going to pause the router-policy canary and switch traffic to legacy routing for eu-west-2. Command: 
```
# pause rollout
kubectl -n infra patch rollout router-policy-canary -p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'
# switch to legacy
routerctl set-policy --env=prod --region=eu-west-2 --policy=legacy-affinity
```

jordan: heads up: switching to legacy may increase cross-AZ hops but should reduce misrouting. Prepare a DR plan if aborting the canary fails.

sam: I've prepped a one-line rollback for infra: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/router-policy --namespace=infra --to-revision=42` — but prefer patching the canary pause first to avoid a full rollback blast.

alex: also enabling target throttling on the ingress LB to stop retries causing queue buildup: `lbctl set-throttle --region=eu-west-2 --max-inflight=200`

maya: adding temporary prefix caching bypass: disable KV cache invalidation for 10m to reduce miss amplification. Patch command: `configctl put /runtime/kvcache/disable_invalidation true`

incident-bot: Update: users impacted: streaming longpolls (customer-facing features) — estimated affected customers: 7 tenants in eu-west-2, severity P1. Postmortem owner assigned: alex.

reyes: paused canary. Policy change applied to route all new sessions via legacy-affinity. Observability: p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 1.2s within 60s on the patched nodes.

jordan: nice. Are we still seeing streaming stalls?

alex: initial reports show fewer stalls, but some sessions are still degraded — likely clients stuck on sessions routed to overloaded hot partitions. We need to evict queued requests and drain hot shards.

sam: plan: 1) mark hot shards readonly; 2) drain with soft-evict to avoid errors; 3) rebalance keys across shards. Command sequence: 
```
shardctl mark-readonly --shard=shard-7 --region=eu-west-2
shardctl drain --shard=shard-7 --grace=30s
shardctl rebalance --region=eu-west-2 --strategy=hash-spread
```

maya: while that's happening, enable fallback replicas for streaming: `streamingctl enable-replica-fallback --region=eu-west-2` — this will route new streams to warm replicas instead of retrying the hot one.

reyes: executing drain on two hot shards now. Observability: queue length halved after first drain. p99 trending down to ~900ms.

oncall-bot: oncall handoff: reyes -> alex in 14m. Please prepare summary and bridge link.

alex: creating bridge: https://calls.example.com/bridge/INC-2026-0421. Adding product and support.

jordan: customer impact note for support: "Customers in eu-west-2 may have experienced streaming stalls and elevated p99 between 14:03-14:12 UTC. Mitigation applied: paused routing canary and drained hot shards."

sam: timeline note: canary start 13:56 UTC, SLO alerts at 14:03, mitigation applied 14:06, p99 < 1.5s by 14:08.

maya: additional telemetry: we saw a small region-skew in route seed distribution — the canary introduced non-uniform weight mapping so a handful of keys ended up concentrated on shard-7/8. That explains hot partitions.

alex: root cause hypothesis: policy change (local-prefer) + weight calculation bug in canary path => skewed hashing -> hot partitions -> retry amplification -> tail latency. Action items: rollback canary, add unit test on weight calc, add canary traffic pattern smoke test for key-distribution.

reyes: I'll open a short-lived task to add the smoke test and ensure the rollout gate blocks if distribution entropy < threshold.

incident-bot: Status update: incident still open, mitigation active, p99 stabilized ~850ms across eu-west-2 but monitoring for 30m. Postmortem template assigned to alex.

sam: any customer escalations? I have a support DM from a major tenant complaining about 2-3 minute stalls; passed to support already — product will follow up.

jordan: let's keep the bridge open until 15:00 UTC. After 30m stable, we can start a controlled canary revert with much smaller traffic.

alex: ACK. I'll collect logs, start postmortem outline, and prepare rollback PR if needed. Thanks all for fast responses. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INC-2026-0421 updated: severity downgraded to P2 if stable after 30m. Next update scheduled in 10m."
